plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero for capital preservation.
This plan prioritizes stability and reduces overall portfolio risk.

conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown risk. Expect slower growth but enhanced stability.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 1% each, and sell SPAL to zero.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure.
Buy XLV at 4% to diversify into a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances growth potential with risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5%/month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and diversifies slightly, offering a blend of growth and stability. Expect moderate drawdowns compared to aggressive modes.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 6% each, leveraging growth.
Buy XLV at 6% to capitalize on a strong scanner setup.
This plan concentrates in high-scoring setups and uses leverage.
Strict stop discipline is crucial for managing increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth approach targets ~4%/month, stretching for higher returns. It significantly increases leveraged ETF exposure and concentration, which amplifies both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs; strict stops are essential to manage substantial risk.

plan: Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book for increased income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.

income.read: This income-focused approach targets ~1%/month, prioritizing yield and capital preservation. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged holdings, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fluctuate, and income is not guaranteed.
